newsitem.title: UK: Brazil fixtures dominate sugar freight market.
newsitem.headline: Brazil fixtures dominate sugar freight market.

text.p: Fixtures from south Brazil formed the mainstay of London's sugar freight market at the end of the week, shipbrokers said on Friday.

Glencore was said to have covered 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from south Brazil to Karachi for early June at around $42 and fixed a prompt 13/14,000-tonne bulk cargo from east coast Mexico to Med/Black Sea.
Swaziland Sugar fixed around 14,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Maputo to London at a rate thought to be slightly above $24 but no more details were available.
Cargill was said to have fixed 25,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Santos to the Black Sea/Baltic/Egyptian Med for mid-June shipment.
Genoc was firm with 14,000 tonnes in bags from Santos to the Red Sea/Indian Ocean for the first half of June.
Of the day's new orders, Amerop quoted for 15,300 tonnes in bulk from Barahona to US Gulf/Atlantic for the second half of June.
Louis Dreyfus was open for 14,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from west coast Guatemala to Black Sea/Baltic for prompt shipment.
